subject: ventures/epoxy-garage-floor-bid-calculator
professional: a senior epoxy / polyaspartic floor-coating contractor who bids residential garages; they check first the material order (gallons per coat from coverage = 1604 x solids / mils, kits, flake bags at 0.15-0.25 lb/sf full broadcast), grind hours for the crew and machine, how many trips the system needs (1-day polyaspartic vs 2-day epoxy flake vs 2-3 day metallic), moisture-barrier and patch labour, and whether margin is taken on price rather than as a markup on cost

evidence.correctness: Independent Python model (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/6d772762-c35d-5a87-aeb0-eb40c77c23ec/scratchpad/epoxy/model.py), written from trade practice not from calc.mjs: grind hours = slab/rate, coat hours per coat, crack hours, travel = miles/mph, loaded wage = wage x (1+burden), material on slab x (1+waste), overhead on direct cost, price = cost/(1-margin). Compared with node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/6d772762-c35d-5a87-aeb0-eb40c77c23ec/scratchpad/epoxy/run.mjs calling calculateBid with the page defaults (20x20, full flake, full grind 80 sf/h, 20 lf cracks, $45 wage, 22% burden, 30 mi at 35 mph, $0.85/mi, 15% overhead, 35% margin): full flake cost 2,854.70 / price 4,391.84 / 89.6 lb flake; solid epoxy degrease 1,224.53 / 1,883.89; solid full grind 1,439.19 / 2,214.14; polyaspartic 3,345.94 / 5,147.61, all equal to the cent when the model also runs coat hours on the waste-inflated area. Under trade convention (waste is material, not rolled area) the model gives 12.31 h and price 4,328.27 vs the tool's 12.97 h and 4,391.84 (+1.5%), calc.mjs:160. Margin vs markup verified: 35% margin = 53.85% markup on cost; a $1,600 proposal on the default flake job gives -78.42% margin, matching hand arithmetic (1600-2854.70)/1600. Not 4: no coverage/mils model, so the kit line cannot be recomputed from a data sheet.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features exercised in node or by the shipped tests: presets and custom width/length, four systems and four prep methods, crack and pit lines, moisture barrier, travel, loaded labour, overhead, margin, walk-away price, proposed-price check, three warnings (skip-grind, starved-flake, travel-heavy), copy bid summary, share link (share.mjs), printable proposal (proposal.mjs, proposal-terms.mjs), opt-out usage counter (usage.mjs). All work; no TODOs. Served page https://marisstella.app/epoxy-garage-floor-bid-calculator/ returns 200 and served llms.txt is live. Gaps against what a coater expects are scored under fitness/domain, not here.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the subject dir: 118 tests, 118 pass, 0 fail (326 ms). Six seeded mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted with git checkout: margin->markup caught (3 fail); flake pounds on slab not billable area caught (1); moisture barrier on billable area caught (1); travel hours doubled caught (2); skip-grind severity ignoring flake caught (1); starved-flake boundary < -> <= SURVIVED (118 pass). Most catches rest on a single test, and expected values are the author's own numbers.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (289 lines), index.html module script (311-420), vs-a-flat-rate-per-square-foot.test.mjs, README. Pure dependency-free core, validates every input and rejects '1,200' and negatives with a message. Defects: coats override changes labour but not material (calc.mjs:154 vs :169, coating cost identical at coats 3 and 4: 1,276.80); waste inflates coat labour (calc.mjs:160); garage.width/length re-parsed after the fact (calc.mjs:212-213).
evidence.claims: vs-a-flat-rate-per-square-foot.html:68 and :94 (and the FAQ JSON-LD at :13) call $1,743 and $2,073 the 'walk-away price' and say a $1,600 flyer is 'underwater on the one the slab actually needs'. The page's own test (vs-a-flat-rate-per-square-foot.test.mjs:92-93) asserts these against result.price, not breakEvenPrice; the walk-away for that job (solid epoxy, full grind, 0 cracks) is 1,347.30 and for degrease-only 1,132.65, so $1,600 is above walk-away on both and the 'underwater' claim is false. :99 says the job is 'described in its README'; it is not. vs-coatingos.html:13 says the tool models 'flake load and coverage'; coverage is not modelled. Guide checks pass: 400 sf at 80 sf/h = 5.0 h; grind 5.0 h vs coats 6.1 h ('often as many hours'); $1,600 below the default flake walk-away 2,854.70; index FAQ 3 coats/12%/220 vs 2/8%/300 match calc.mjs:25-43. Disclaimer present on every page.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a 2-car full-flake grind bid. A contractor gets a defensible price and walk-away, but cannot get the material order (no gallons, kits or bags of flake: 89.6 lb is shown, gallons are not), and the bid charges one round trip and one person regardless of system, so a 2-day epoxy flake or 3-day metallic is priced with the same travel as a 1-day polyaspartic and a 2-person crew's drive is half-counted. Moisture barrier adds material only, no application hours. Usable as a gut-check, not as the bid sheet.
evidence.domain: Compared with manufacturer practice: coverage = 1604 x volume solids / mils (100% solids at 10 mils = 160.4 sf/gal), full-broadcast flake 0.15-0.25 lb/sf (Torginol-style guidance; the tool's 0.20/0.18 lb/sf and 0.12 starved threshold agree). Departures: kit cost is a bare $/sf with no solids, mils or coats behind it (calc.mjs:25-62), and the polyaspartic default $4.25/sf is roughly 3x a data-sheet build (2 coats, 8 and 10 mils at ~92% solids on 448 sf = 5.0 gal; at an assumed $120/gal = $605, $1.35/sf); return-trip days per system are not modelled though they are the core of the 1-day polyaspartic pitch the guide makes; moisture barrier has no labour; no crew size. Margin-on-price and overhead-on-direct-cost are correct trade practice.

verdict: The arithmetic is right: four jobs recomputed by an independent model match to the cent, margin is taken on price, and 118 tests catch 5 of 6 seeded bugs. It misses the bar on claims: the vs-flat-rate page calls the bid price the walk-away price and so says a $1,600 flyer is underwater when the walk-away is $1,347. A senior coater would also miss a material order (no coverage/mils/gallons, a polyaspartic kit about 3x a data-sheet build), trip days per system (the 1-day polyaspartic point), and moisture-barrier labour. A sound gut-check, not yet the bid sheet.
